title: Taylor Pancaldi Technology Services
shortDescription: Bilingual Catalan–English landing page for my engineering company
mediumDescription: The static Astro landing page for my company's two engineering practices, Catalan first and English second. Both languages implement one typed Copy interface, so a missing or renamed key in either is a type error rather than a silently untranslated page.

title: FlexTag
shortDescription: Asset register for a small consultancy, with QR labels printed straight to a Brother label printer
mediumDescription: What do we own, what did it cost, when did we buy it, and where's the invoice? FlexTag answers those for my company's hardware, and prints the QR labels that go on it – scan one with a phone to open its page. It's an exercise in professional-grade Python: a FastAPI and PostgreSQL API under mypy --strict, a phone-first Next.js frontend, and a separate service driving a Brother QL-800, with idempotency keys so a retry never produces a second sticker.

title: LinkedIn Games Unlimited
shortDescription: Unlimited Queens and Tango, with generated boards and difficulty measured by the logic they force
mediumDescription: Clones of LinkedIn's daily Queens and Tango puzzles with generators that make as many boards as you want. Both work backwards from a finished grid; naively generated Queens boards are uniquely solvable only about 1% of the time, so instead of rerolling, each rival solution is killed by moving a single cell into another region – taking the yield to 31–59%. Difficulty is rated by the hardest deduction a logical solver is forced to use, the same ladder powers hints that explain rather than spoil, and a check proves no board ever needs a guess. Two offline-capable Next.js PWAs in a pnpm workspace, each deployed independently on Netlify.

title: Andorra Coaches
shortDescription: Every coach between Andorra and the airports, from both operators, on one screen
mediumDescription: Two operators run coaches between Andorra and Barcelona or Toulouse, each with its own site and search. This merges both into one chronological list with prices and seats where available, and links out to each operator's own booking page – no payments, no personal data, no logins. Neither operator has a public API, so each is wrapped in an adapter built from careful reconnaissance, running in a Cloudflare Worker behind a React PWA designed to be read at arm's length in an airport. Offline tests run against captured real responses, and weekly live contract tests fail with the exact anchor that moved.

title: Postilla
shortDescription: Self-hosted comment system for static blogs, rewritten from the ground up after Waline
mediumDescription: A self-hosted comment system for static blogs: an embeddable Vue widget, a moderation dashboard, and a Fastify and PostgreSQL API that serves both. It began as my fork of Waline and became a full rewrite once LeanCloud, its default datastore, announced its shutdown. The architecture is hexagonal with the boundaries enforced by lint rules, schemas are declared once in zod and become types, client and OpenAPI, and the design decisions – one database instead of nine, revocable sessions instead of a forever-JWT, an outbox without a queue library – are written up as ADRs. Feature-complete; cutover from the legacy deployment is next.

title: Carouselizer
shortDescription: Figma plugin that turns a YAML file into a ready-made Instagram carousel
mediumDescription: A Figma plugin that builds Instagram carousels from a YAML or JSON file using the components already in the file. It auto-fits body text, splits slides that can't fit at a readable size by measuring candidates in a real frame, supports text, list, quote and stat slides, and previews everything before touching the document.

title: A punt companion
shortDescription: A study-first audio player for the A punt Catalan course, with a transcript for every track
mediumDescription: A self-hosted player for the audio of the A punt Catalan course, built for studying rather than listening: tracks stop when they end, with repeat, A–B loops, speeds down to 0.6× and the transcript for every track. The app is one self-contained HTML file installed as a PWA and served over Tailscale. The Python preprocessing splits multi-column transcript PDFs by measuring each page's gutters from word positions, landing 98–99% of the text in the right track across 292 tracks.

title: Hoy Hablamos player
shortDescription: A private study app for nearly 3,000 Spanish podcast episodes and their transcripts
mediumDescription: Podcast apps are built for keeping up with the newest episode, not for studying a back catalogue. This private PWA holds all 2,961 episodes of the Hoy Hablamos Spanish podcast I have access to – about 35 GB of audio – with search, filters by series and listening status, star ratings, a speed-adjustable player, offline downloads and the transcript beside every episode. A single self-contained HTML file served over Tailscale, with Python scripts that fetch episodes and build the catalogue.

title: gymextract
shortDescription: Exports Technogym workout data as JSON, with a training dashboard on top
mediumDescription: Technogym equipment logs every set, rep and treadmill second to mywellness.com, and there's no usable public API to get it back. This Python CLI uses the portal's internal endpoints to export each session as clean JSON – sets, weights, muscle scores and per-second cardio series – and replacing an HTML scrape with the structured data already in the session payload took strength-set capture from 0 of 75 exercises to 75 of 75. A daily launchd sync feeds a small React dashboard of strength progression, muscle balance and visit cadence.

title: Language Transfer Companion
shortDescription: Unofficial companion to the Language Transfer audio courses: per-track topic lists and downloadable flashcards
mediumDescription: Language Transfer offers free audio language courses that teach you to think in a new language, with nothing to read and nothing to memorise. This unofficial companion adds the two things the audio doesn't come with: a searchable topic list for every track, so you can find or review a lesson, and downloadable CSV flashcard decks for when you do want to drill the vocabulary. Spanish, German, Italian and French are covered so far. Built with Astro as a fully prerendered static site – no client-side framework.

title: FlexInvoice
shortDescription: A self-hosted invoicing tool: YAML data in, a single PDF with the invoice and its expense receipts out
mediumDescription: As a new freelancer managing my own company, I needed tailored invoices without Word templates or a full accounting suite. What began as a React template printed to PDF with Puppeteer is now a small self-hosted stack: a Next.js rendering engine, and a React GUI and Python CLI backed by plain YAML data. Presets fill in the recurring parts, expenses import from bank CSVs, and their receipts – PDFs or photos – are merged into the same PDF as the invoice. It all deploys from pinned Docker images.

title: Appetize.io 2.0
shortDescription: Rebranding of our company's website, built from scratch using AstroJS
mediumDescription: In early 2025, the company I work for decided to redesign its marketing website. The previous version was visually appealing but too playful for our business-focused audience. The new appetize.io was rebuilt almost from scratch, embracing a more dynamic and modern design. We leveraged the latest web technologies to enhance speed, accessibility, and SEO, ensuring a polished and professional experience tailored to our users.

title: All-Star Advent of Code
shortDescription: My submissions to all Advent of Code challenges (2015-2024)
mediumDescription: Advent of Code is a yearly event offering Christmas-themed coding challenges. After completing the 2020 event, I decided to tackle puzzles from previous years. Thanks to these I've gained proficiency in Kotlin and refined my problem-solving skills, and I'm quite proud of my shiny 500 stars ⭐. As a side project, I developed an API automating class setup for daily challenges, fetching input data, and updating my progress on the Readme.

title: AI Job Search
shortDescription: Claude-driven pipeline that turns a job description into a grounded, tailored CV and cover letter
mediumDescription: Paste a job description and get back a fit assessment, a tailored CV, a cover letter and drafted screening answers – all rendered to PDFs that match the Word-authored CV they replace. Every generated line has to cite an id from a corpus of real experience, and three Node scripts enforce that mechanically: unknown ids and uncited claims are rejected, house style and AI tells are flagged, and the rendered PDF is checked for text layer, reading order and keyword coverage. Anything that can't be traced back to the corpus gets deleted rather than softened.

title: conju.gat
shortDescription: Catalan verb conjugation trainer where colour and shape encode which of 85 patterns a verb follows, across ten tenses
mediumDescription: Learning Catalan, I found myself colour-coding verbs in my notes to tell the irregulars apart; conju.gat turns that habit into the whole interface. Each of the 8,500+ verbs carries a Miró-inspired colour-and-shape sign encoding which of 85 conjugation patterns it follows. Three study modes (look up a paradigm, conjugate aloud and self-check, or type all six forms) share one full-screen, and progress is tracked per verb and tense to prioritise what you get wrong.

title: Media Library Tools
shortDescription: Verifiable batch MP3 tag editing, built while rescuing a 12,000-track library
mediumDescription: A Python toolkit for batch-editing tags across a large MP3 library without corrupting it. It diagnoses why albums split, fixes tag spam and mixed ID3 versions, and generates portable playlists – but the real feature is the safety core: every write dry-runs by default, backs up the original, and proves the audio bytes are untouched by hashing the MPEG payload with all tag containers stripped. You can't verify a tag write by comparing duration, which shifts on VBR files even when the audio is intact.

title: IDE Portfolio
shortDescription: An experiment in rendering a developer portfolio as a code editor
mediumDescription: A portfolio that presents itself as an IDE: a file tree of index.tsx, about.md and cv.tsx, a tab bar, a status bar showing branch and build state, and a ⌘K command palette for navigating between "files". Built with Astro and React islands, with light and dark themes – the light one took longer, since a syntax palette designed for a dark editor collapses to unreadable contrast when you simply invert the background.

title: Italy Job Hunter
shortDescription: Fork of an AI job-hunting pipeline, retuned for signal quality over model quality
mediumDescription: A fork of Simone Camerano's Italy Job Hunter, which searches the web with Tavily, triages results with a fast Groq model, analyses the survivors against your CV with DeepSeek-V3, and pushes match reports to Telegram. My additions target the false positives: a career-scan mode that visits curated company career pages directly with headless Playwright and reports only unseen postings, a day-of-week partitioned site list, geo-restriction triage for "remote" roles that aren't, and filters for stale results, forum hosts and login-walled domains.

title: Linkarium
shortDescription: Drop your links, share the list – shareable link lists with automatic metadata scraping
mediumDescription: Paste a pile of URLs, or a block of prose with links buried in it, and get back a clean shareable page with titles, descriptions, favicons and preview images already filled in – YouTube links get their real title and channel name too, via oEmbed. No signup needed to read a list. Built with Next.js 16, Supabase and Tailwind CSS 4 on Vercel, localised in English and Italian. The fiddliest part was the least glamorous: extracting URLs from arbitrary pasted text, where trailing punctuation and sentence parentheses quietly produce valid-but-wrong links.

title: LinkedIn Job Filter
shortDescription: Chrome extension that flags misleading "remote" job ads before you read them
mediumDescription: An AI job-ad analyser that watches the LinkedIn job panel and injects a colour-coded verdict into each listing, with red flags, positives and key facts at a glance. Its headline check is the location reality check: does this "remote" role actually require local residency? Runs on Google Gemini's free tier or on a fully private local model via Ollama. Timezone comparisons are deliberately done in code rather than by the model – asking an LLM to do arithmetic on MST vs CET is a reliable way to get a confident wrong answer.

title: RapidAnd Order Tracker
shortDescription: Telegram bot tracking supplier orders, designed to be a polite client of someone else's API
mediumDescription: A Telegram bot that tracks orders on a supplier platform, written to avoid logging into a web app several times a day. The design constraint was staying a polite client of an API that isn't mine: it's manual-refresh by default, answering most commands from a local SQLite cache with no network call at all, behind a cooldown, a cache TTL and a hard daily call cap. Built with TypeScript, grammY and Zod, shipped as a Docker container running on a home NAS.

title: Anki flashcard decks
shortDescription: Hand-built language flashcard decks kept as plain CSV, in Git rather than in an app
mediumDescription: A growing collection of flashcard decks built while learning Spanish, French, Italian, German and now Catalan – around 600 hand-compiled thematic vocabulary cards, decks aligned to the Language Transfer audio courses and split by course part, and 800 Italian–Catalan cards following the units of the A punt coursebook, so a deck always maps onto what you've actually studied. Deliberately boring: no app, no schema, no build step. Two columns of comma-separated text in Git outlive whichever flashcard app I'm using this year. This repo is where Language Transfer Companion came from.

title: Purrfect Price
shortDescription: Compare cat food prices from top sellers with Purrfect Price
mediumDescription: Purrfect Price is a tool built with NextJS, using Playwright to scrape popular cat food seller websites and AgGrid to organize, filter, and compare the best deals on various cat food brands. Whether searching for budget-friendly options or premium products, Purrfect Price helps you find the best deals effortlessly.

title: McGraw-Hill Flashcard Exporter
shortDescription: Go tool that exports McGraw-Hill Language Lab flashcards as per-chapter CSV
mediumDescription: McGraw-Hill publishes free companion flashcards for its language books through a web Language Lab that has no export, so you can't fold them into the spaced-repetition app you already use. This Go program downloads them and writes one CSV per chapter, ready to import into Anki or Brainscape – HTML stripped, chapter numbers zero-padded so files sort correctly, and the site's hidden "Other" language menu expanded automatically. No dependencies beyond the standard library.

title: Real estate scraper
shortDescription: Configurable multi-site property scraper, driven by selectors stored in SQLite
mediumDescription: House hunting across two countries means comparing listings on a dozen portals, none of which export anything. This started as a pair of Python scrapers for Immobiliare and Idealista and grew into a configurable multi-site engine: CSS selectors, URL patterns and pagination rules live in SQLite tables rather than in code, so adding a new estate agent means inserting rows, not writing Python. Idealista fronts everything with bot protection – the practical lesson being that scraping is easy and staying unblocked is the whole problem.

My team now uses the toolbar daily, and I'm expanding its functionality to allow other teams to easily configure their own settings.
